## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished web game where the player is a great white shark hunting underwater, with ships occasionally passing on the surface.
- Deliver a visually strong, playable Three.js experience with responsive desktop/mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Theme: great white shark, underwater hunting, surface ships.
- Should be visually beautiful and polished; user did not specify framework, so Three.js was chosen.
- Must work on desktop and mobile with touch controls.

## Decisions
- Built a Vite + Three.js app with all visuals generated procedurally; no external 3D assets.
- Game title/branding: **APEX — THE GREAT WHITE**.
- Gameplay: eat fish and seals, maintain hunger/vitality, build combo, avoid ship propeller wash, reach 6 seals.
- Menu, HUD, pause, win/loss overlays, radar, touch joystick/buttons, and procedural audio were implemented.
- Camera changed from dead-behind to an over-the-shoulder rear-quarter angle so the shark silhouette is readable.
- Fixed reverse body triangle winding after discovering the camera was seeing the body’s culled/internal surfaces and the jaw cavity.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolded with `package.json`, Vite, Three.js dependencies.
- `index.html`, full HUD/menu/pause/end markup, and extensive responsive CSS completed.
- Procedural shark model, animated tail/jaw, fins, teeth, eyes, gills.
- Procedural ocean surface shader, sky, seafloor, caustics, kelp, rocks, light shafts, marine snow, bubbles, blood, splash, fish schools, seals, and cargo/trawler/yacht ships.
- Main game loop, scoring, hunger, vitality, combo, radar, targeting reticle, controls, menu/gameplay/pause/end flow, procedural audio.
- Dev server running via tmux session `apex` on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser installed and functioning; screenshots taken in `screenshots/`.
- Identified and fixed shark mesh winding with `indices.push(a, b, c, b, d, c)`; final visual verification of this fix is still pending.

### Active
- Verify the shark now renders correctly after the winding fix.
- Refine remaining model/visual issues: tail fin shape, mouth read, ship silhouettes, and overall underwater composition.
- Test actual hunting, biting, seal/fish consumption, breach behavior, pause/restart, and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Open `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/shark-crop5.png` to verify the winding fix corrected the hollow-body/jaw artifact.
2. Recheck full gameplay and menu screenshots at 1440×900 and 390×844.
3. Exercise gameplay: turn, rise/dive, boost, breach, bite fish/seals, score/hunger/radar, pause, restart, win/loss.
4. Polish weak visuals if needed, especially tail silhouette, mouth, fish/seal visibility, and distant ship silhouettes.
5. Run `npm run build` and verify no runtime console errors.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Core game state, controls, camera, HUD, radar, targeting, scene boot, debug API.
- `src/world.js`: Ocean, sky, seafloor, particles, fish, seals, ships, world update and collision helpers.
- `src/shark.js`: Procedural shark model and animations.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural WebAudio ambience and sound effects.
- `src/style.css`: Full menu/HUD/overlay responsive styling.
- `index.html`: App markup and overlays.
- `package.json`: Vite/Three.js project config.
- `screenshots/`: Menu/game/test screenshots for visual inspection.
- `dist/`: Production build output from `npm run build`.

## Important Context
- Winding bug found: body indices were originally `indices.push(a, c, b, b, c, d)`, which made normals inward and caused the mouth jaw to appear through the body. Changed to `indices.push(a, b, c, b, d, c)`; not yet visually confirmed.
- `world.js` `Seal` constructor stores `seal.initial`; reset logic in `main.js` depends on it.
- `window.__APEX__.state` exposes debug state; `window.__APEX__.inspect` exposes `{ camera, shark, player, scene, renderer }`.
- Current camera: behind `-9.4`, right offset `5.4`, height `3.15`, look-ahead `8.7`.
- Current game start state: shark at `(0,-12.5,4)`, depth ~13 m, hunger 82, goal 6 seals.
- Playwright commands used: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`, `playwright-cli click '#start-btn'`, `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=<absolute path>`.
- Build warning only: Vite chunk >500 kB.
- No commits have been made for the new game files; they remain uncommitted/untracked.

## Objective
- Build a polished web game where the player is a great white shark hunting underwater, with ships occasionally passing on the surface.
- Deliver a visually strong, playable Three.js experience with responsive desktop/mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Theme: great white shark, underwater hunting, surface ships.
- Must be visually beautiful/polished and work on desktop and mobile with touch controls.
- User did not specify a framework; Three.js was chosen.

## Decisions
- Built a Vite + Three.js app with all visuals generated procedurally; no external 3D assets.
- Game branding: **APEX — THE GREAT WHITE**.
- Gameplay: eat fish and seals, maintain hunger/vitality, build combo, avoid ship propeller wash, collect 6 seals to win.
- Menu, HUD, pause, win/loss overlays, radar, touch joystick/buttons, and procedural audio implemented.
- Camera made lower and side-offset for a cinematic three-quarter shark view; portrait and landscape layouts adapted.
- Rewrote shark model with lofted body, sharper snout, crescent tail, swept fins, visible mouth/teeth, and corrected jaw hinge.
- Added nearby bait fish and a closer first seal to improve onboarding.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game scaffold, HTML markup, responsive CSS, HUD/menu/overlays.
- Procedural shark, animated tail/jaw/fins, eyes, gills, scars, mouth/teeth.
- Ocean surface shader, sky, seafloor, caustics, kelp, rocks, light shafts, marine snow, bubbles, blood, splash, fish schools, seals, cargo/trawler/yacht ships.
- Main game loop, scoring, hunger, vitality, combo, radar, targeting reticle, controls, pause/end/win flow, procedural audio.
- Fixed shark winding; rebuilt jaw so mouth opening rotates downward instead of through the body roof.
- Added 6th seal so the 6-seal goal is achievable.
- Reworked fish into silver, tapered fish geometry; increased visibility and adjusted flee behavior.
- Tuned hunger drain, seal flee speed, bite radius, camera framing, and mobile/landscape HUD layout.
- Added favicon and fixed mobile nav display.
- Verified fish bite, seal bite, 6-seal win flow, breach camera, pause overlay, desktop/mobile/landscape screenshots.
- `npm run build` succeeds; only Vite chunk-size warning remains.
- Dev server running in tmux session `apex` at `http://localhost:3002`.

### Active
- Final visual review/cleanup remains; core game is playable and tested.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Review remaining minor polish opportunities, especially shark body contrast, tail silhouette, and mobile target-reticle placement.
2. Run one final `npm run build` and browser smoke test after any last edits.
3. Optionally update `README.md` with game controls and run instructions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game state, controls, camera, HUD, radar, targeting, scene boot, debug API.
- `src/world.js`: Ocean, sky, seafloor, particles, fish, seals, ships, world update and collision helpers.
- `src/shark.js`: Procedural shark model and animations.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural WebAudio ambience and sound effects.
- `src/style.css`: Menu/HUD/overlay responsive styling.
- `index.html`: App markup and overlays.
- `public/favicon.svg`: Browser favicon.
- `package.json`: Vite/Three.js project config.
- `screenshots/`: Visual verification captures.
- `dist/`: Production build output.

## Important Context
- `window.__APEX__.state` exposes debug state; `window.__APEX__.inspect` exposes `{ camera, shark, player, scene, renderer, world }`; debug helpers include `start`, `bite`, and `breach`.

- Seal flee interpolation is now `dt * 0.38`; seal bite radius `6.1`; hunger drain `0.55 + boosting 0.6`.
